## Description
Expands the OctoAcme project management personas documentation to include six additional critical roles that support cross-functional project delivery. This addresses gaps in role clarity, accountability, and integration of QA, governance, technical, design, team management, and agile coaching functions.

## Changes
- **Updated file**: `docs/octoacme-roles-and-personas.md`
- **New personas added**:
  - QA/Testing Lead - Quality strategy, test planning, and acceptance validation
  - Stakeholder/Sponsor - Business outcomes and governance oversight
  - Technical Lead/Architect - Technical design decisions and risk management
  - Design Lead/UX Researcher - User experience and usability validation
  - Tech Lead Manager - Team capacity and career development bridging
  - Scrum Master/Agile Coach - Agile ceremonies and process improvement

## Why This Change
Current project management documentation only defines four primary personas (Developers, Product Managers, Project Managers, and general overview). Many OctoAcme projects involve additional critical roles that aren't formally documented, creating:

- **Clarity issues**: New team members lack guidance on QA, UX, technical strategy, and governance responsibilities
- **Accountability gaps**: No documented expectations for stakeholders, sponsors, and technical leads
- **Integration confusion**: Processes reference these roles but don't explain how they interact with core roles
- **Onboarding friction**: Cross-functional teams lack persona-based guidance

## Impact
- ✅ Clearer role definitions reduce confusion on multi-disciplinary teams
- ✅ Improved project governance through explicit sponsor/stakeholder participation
- ✅ Enhanced quality through documented QA leadership responsibilities
- ✅ Better technical decision-making with architect/tech lead accountability
- ✅ Stronger team dynamics through UX and design integration
- ✅ More effective agile execution through formalized scrum master guidance

Closes #4: Adding more personas and roles to the project management processes
